final_recommendation: The room converged on a comprehensive trilateral package: 75% auto RVC with January 1, 2020 grace period for pre-2020 vehicles; Chapter 23 labor enforcement with quarterly inspections, 30-day remedy windows, and automatic tariff snapback; phased dairy tariff cuts (3.25%/6.5%/9.75% capped over three years); Chapter 19 dispute settlement preserved; and a year-three auto-renewal mechanism replacing the hard sunset clause. USTR committed to WTO filing within 90 minutes, with Canada and Mexico signing contingent on redline delivery.
minority_objections: Auto industry initially resisted immediate January 2020 implementation without phase-in runway
Canada initially refused any dairy concessions as a red line before accepting phased caps
key_conflicts: Canada's Chapter 19 preservation vs. U.S. preference to eliminate it (resolved: Chapter 19 stays)
Hard sunset clause creating business uncertainty vs. need for modernization mechanism (resolved: year-three review with auto-renewal)
Labor enforcement teeth vs. Mexico's sovereignty concerns on complaint mechanisms (resolved: parallel filing with independent inspections)
Immediate auto RVC implementation vs. supply chain adjustment needs (resolved: 90-day grace for pre-2020 vehicles)
key_concessions: Canada accepted phased dairy market access (3.25%/6.5%/9.75% capped) despite initial red line
Mexico accepted independent labor inspections and parallel worker complaint filing
U.S. accepted Chapter 19 preservation and year-three auto-renewal mechanism instead of hard sunset
Auto industry accepted January 1, 2020 implementation with only 90-day grace period
red_lines: Canada: Chapter 19 dispute settlement must remain intact (preserved in final text)
Canada: Supply management cannot be gutted (resolved via capped phased access)
Labor unions/Congress: Enforceable labor inspections with automatic tariff snapback (locked in Chapter 23)
Mexico: Worker complaints cannot bypass Mexican labor ministry entirely (resolved via parallel notification)
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Implementation capacity for quarterly inspections across Mexican factories not discussed
Political sustainability of dairy concessions in Canadian Parliament beyond initial ratification
Supply chain disruption costs during 90-day grace period transition not quantified
Enforcement mechanism for year-three review process if parties disagree on renewal
downstream_risk_variables: Congressional ratification timeline pressure (pre-midterms deadline mentioned)
Mexican labor ministry capacity to process parallel complaints within 30-day remedy windows
Auto industry capital commitment decisions hinge on WTO filing finality
Canadian Parliament vote contingent on exact Chapter 19 and dairy language in redline
uncertainty_notes: Redline text delivery pending within 90 minutes of R7 close; actual WTO filing and Parliamentary tabling not yet confirmed complete; enforcement implementation details for Chapter 23 quarterly inspections (inspection team composition, factory selection criteria) not specified; year-three review mechanism procedural rules undefined.

marker_evidence.auto_rules_bottleneck: 75% RVC implementation date and grace period drove multiple rounds of negotiation; auto_industry's capital commitment decisions were explicitly contingent on resolution; USTR's January 2020 lock forced the 90-day grace compromise that unblocked the package
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_key: Chapter 23 enforcement language (quarterly inspections, 30-day remedy, automatic tariff snapback) was Congress's explicit ratification condition; labor_union stated 'Congress won't ratify it, and neither will my membership' without teeth; drove parallel-filing compromise and final redline locks
marker_evidence.canada_dairy_final_issue: Canada initially stated dairy 'isn't a bargaining chip—it's a red line'; USTR's ultimatum ('sign this with Mexico and you're outside') forced the phased tariff compromise (3.25/6.5/9.75 capped); dairy_ag confirmed 'my members are satisfied' only after caps locked in text
marker_evidence.dispute_settlement_canada_redline: Canada stated Chapter 19 'aren't negotiating positions, they're political red lines' and demanded written confirmation in redline; however, USTR confirmed preservation early and it did not block progress—acknowledged as non-negotiable but not a bottleneck
marker_evidence.sunset_to_review_compromise: Supply_chain_mfr stated manufacturers 'can't commit capital to retooling for 75% RVC if the agreement itself sunsets in five years'; drove the year-three review with auto-renewal mechanism that replaced hard sunset; explicit stated reason for the compromise structure
marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Congress explicitly conditioned floor vote on redline delivery ('I'm not moving this to the floor without seeing the actual enforcement text'); labor_union tied membership support to enforcement teeth; Canada tied Parliament vote to Chapter 19 and dairy language; drove multiple text-locking demands
marker_evidence.supply_chain_adjustment: Auto_industry and supply_chain_mfr raised sourcing freeze dates and retooling timelines as concerns ('nine-month capex decision I can't reverse'); however, these were accommodated via the grace period without changing the core RVC structure—noted but not decisive
marker_evidence.us_mexico_first_pressures_canada: USTR's repeated ultimatum ('we sign this with Mexico and you're outside looking in') explicitly leveraged the bilateral-first structure; Canada_min acknowledged 'a bilateral you struck without us at the table'; drove Canada's dairy concession and timeline pressure for signature
